source: npm pack @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory@2026.8.31, tarball extracted and dist/index.js read (not installed, not executed)

create_entities.rationale: Appends agent-supplied entities and echoes back only the newly added subset (omission reveals only whether an agent-guessed name exists).

create_relations.rationale: Appends agent-supplied relations and echoes back only the newly added subset.

add_observations.rationale: Adds agent-supplied observations and echoes back the added strings (error echoes the agent-supplied entity name).

delete_entities.rationale: Deletes by name; returns a fixed string.

delete_observations.rationale: Deletes observations; returns a fixed string.

delete_relations.rationale: Deletes relations; returns a fixed string.

read_graph.rationale: Returns the entire graph: returns entities/relations persisted in the host JSONL memory file (non-public user data accumulated across sessions).

search_nodes.rationale: Substring search that returns entities/relations persisted in the host JSONL memory file (non-public user data accumulated across sessions).

open_nodes.rationale: Returns named entities and adjacent relations: returns entities/relations persisted in the host JSONL memory file (non-public user data accumulated across sessions).

notes: Storage: MEMORY_FILE_PATH env var if set (absolute as-is; relative resolved against the package's dist/ directory), else <package>/dist/memory.jsonl, i.e. inside the npx cache when launched via npx; legacy memory.json is migrated (dist/index.js:11-43, 494-496). MEMORY_FILE_PATH only relocates storage and removes no tool or label, so it is not a value condition.

SECRET decision: the knowledge graph is a host file holding facts about the user/projects that the agent chose to persist; it is non-public data, and read_graph/search_nodes/open_nodes return it, which fits the 'host files' clause of SECRET. Always enabled, so the package union is always {SECRET}.

UNTRUSTED decision (primary): not assigned. The graph is a local single-writer store; within a session any injected text it could return is already in context via the tool that first delivered it, and cross-session poisoning from an earlier injected session is excluded because PREREG's primary model says the attacker does not control the user's local data. This matches server-filesystem, where the agent can also write files that are read back later.
Secondary variant: not assigned. The graph is not a user-credential store that end users or collaborators can write (Supabase/Postgres/GitHub private data), so secondary_extra is empty.

No SINK: every write goes only to the local JSONL file via temp file + rename (dist/index.js:82-116); there is no network code. The server also exposes the graph as the MCP resource memory://knowledge-graph (dist/index.js:463-480); it is not a tool.
